summary: Defines a simple protocol by which management information for a network element can be inspected or altered by remote users. It works with companion memos on structure and the MIB. It was replaced by RFC 1098.

eli5.summary: A way to ask a router or computer "how are you?" from far away and, if allowed, tell it to change a setting.

questions: how does simple network management protocol work
subtitle: A simple protocol for managing network devices by inspecting and changing their status.

tldr.problem: As networks grew, operators needed a way to check the health and status of routers, switches, and servers, and to configure them remotely without logging into each one.
tldr.mechanism: SNMP defines a set of operations (get, set, and trap) that allow a management station to query or change variables on a managed device. A lightweight agent on each device responds to these requests, and can also send unsolicited notifications (traps) when problems occur.
tldr.outcome: SNMP became the de facto standard for network management, widely deployed on routers, switches, servers, and network appliances. RFC 1067 was quickly superseded by RFC 1098, and later by SNMPv3 (RFC 3410), but the core model remains unchanged.

today: RFC 1067 is a draft standard that was superseded by RFC 1098. SNMPv3 (RFC 3410) added security features, but SNMPv1 and SNMPv2 remain the most widely deployed. SNMP is the de facto standard for network management on the Internet.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
RFC 1067 defines the Simple Network Management Protocol (SNMP), a protocol by which management information for a network element can be inspected or altered by a remote management station. SNMP works together with the Structure of Management Information (SMI) and the Management Information Base (MIB) to provide a complete architecture for managing TCP/IP networks.

SNMP is explicitly designed to be simple. The protocol minimizes the number and complexity of functions that a managed device must implement, reducing development cost and allowing management tools to be rich and sophisticated. The protocol uses UDP for transport, sending each message as a single datagram, which allows it to operate even when network conditions are poor.
sections.eli5: SNMP is a simple way to ask network devices questions and tell them what to do. The device doesn't need to be very smart; the management computer does all the thinking.

sections.title: The Management Architecture
sections.content:
SNMP defines a relationship between two kinds of systems. A manager (typically a network operations center) sends commands to agents on managed devices (routers, switches, servers). Agents respond to four basic request types: GetRequest (read a variable), GetNextRequest (read the next variable in the MIB), SetRequest (write a variable), and Trap (an unsolicited notification).

Each agent belongs to a community, identified by a community name. Communities define administrative relationships and access control; a manager belonging to the same community can read or write the agent's variables. This concept allows a single agent to support multiple managers in different administrative domains with different access rights.
sections.eli5: Think of a manager as someone in the control room and an agent as a device on the network. The manager asks the agent questions, the agent answers, and if something breaks, the agent sends a message.

sections.title: Protocol Data Units and Operations
sections.content:
SNMP messages consist of a version number, a community name, and a protocol data unit (PDU). The GetRequest PDU asks for the value of one or more variables identified by their object names. The GetNextRequest PDU returns the name and value of the next variable in the management information base, allowing a manager to walk through a table one row at a time. The GetResponse PDU contains the requested values or an error code.

The SetRequest PDU asks the agent to set one or more variables to new values. The agent responds with GetResponse, either confirming the change or indicating an error (e.g., badValue if the new value is invalid, or readOnly if the variable cannot be modified). The Trap PDU is sent by an agent without being requested, to announce an event such as a cold start (reboot), a link going down or up, or an authentication failure.
sections.eli5: GetRequest says "tell me the value of this variable." GetNextRequest says "tell me the next one." SetRequest says "change this to a new value." Trap says "something happened."

sections.title: Management Model and MIB
sections.content:
SNMP models all management as reading and writing variables. The variables live in the Management Information Base (MIB), which is a conceptual tree of named objects. Each object is identified by a unique name (an ASN.1 OBJECT IDENTIFIER), and each object has a value and a type. The SMI defines how to describe these objects in a standard way.

Common managed objects include system information (description, uptime, contact), interface statistics (packets sent, received, or dropped on each port), routing table entries, TCP connection states, and EGP neighbor status. The MIB is extensible; vendors can define private objects for their own products. The structure allows table-like objects (e.g., the routing table) to be queried a row at a time using GetNextRequest.
sections.eli5: Everything on the network device is represented as a variable. The management station reads and writes these variables. A router might have variables for "how many packets arrived on port 1" or "what's the routing table."

sections.title: Design Principles and Simplicity
sections.content:
SNMP minimizes agent complexity so that even modems, bridges, and other simple devices can support management. Instead of supporting rich imperative commands, SNMP provides only get and set operations. If a manager wants to reboot a device, it sets a variable (e.g., "seconds until reboot") rather than sending a "reboot" command. This design shifts complexity from the agent to the manager and the management tools.

SNMP relies on polling and a limited number of traps. A manager periodically polls agents for status, and agents send traps only for important events. This reduces network traffic and avoids overwhelming managers with unsolicited messages. The use of UDP datagrams instead of TCP connections also keeps the protocol simple and allows it to work in degraded network conditions.
sections.eli5: Instead of asking the device to do something complicated, you just set a variable to tell it what to do. If you want it to reboot in 60 seconds, you set a variable that says that.

sections.title: Status and Standardization
sections.content:
RFC 1067 was published in August 1988 as a draft standard for the Internet. It was quickly superseded by RFC 1098, which made minor refinements, and later by SNMPv2 and SNMPv3 (RFC 3410), which added security and community-string-free authentication. However, SNMPv1 remains widely deployed.

The IAB designated SNMP as "Draft Standard" alongside CMOT (RFC 1095), with the expectation that SNMP would be the short-term protocol and CMOT the long-term direction. In practice, SNMP's simplicity and CMOT's complexity led SNMP to become the dominant network management protocol. Today, virtually every network device supports SNMP, making it the lingua franca of network operations.
sections.eli5: SNMP was designed as a quick fix while they worked on a more powerful system called CMOT. SNMP turned out to be so practical that it's still the standard everyone uses today.
